documentation: String is registered as a native external class with exactly one known property (length) — almost everything else on String has no dedicated codegen. Audited against Emitter.kt's String-specific branches plus the generic NUMERIC_CAST_NAMES/emitIndex paths that silently (and sometimes wrongly) apply to a String receiver too.

declarations.name: length
declarations.documentation: Lua's # length operator — same mechanism as List/Set/Map .size

declarations.name: get
limitations: Lua strings aren't indexable with [] (a string's metatable routes __index to the string library, not characters) — s[0] silently compiles to the List-style s[1] shift and returns nil instead of erroring or returning a character. A real correctness gap, not just a missing feature.

declarations.name: contains
declarations.documentation: string.find(s, x, 1, true) — plain literal substring search, also reachable via the general `x in s` infix operator

declarations.name: hashCode
limitations: A hand-written FNV/Java-style string hash loop — produces a stable, collision-safe-enough value for this transpiler's own internal use, but does NOT match the real JVM String.hashCode() integer value

declarations.name: toInt
limitations: No-op pass-through (the string's own Lua text, unchanged) — relies entirely on Lua's implicit string-to-number coercion in arithmetic contexts; breaks under ==, tostring(), string.format("%d", ...), or anything that cares the value is a real Lua number and not a string

declarations.name: toDouble
limitations: Same no-op pass-through caveat as toInt()

declarations.name: toFloat
limitations: Same no-op pass-through caveat as toInt()

declarations.name: toLong
limitations: Same no-op pass-through caveat as toInt()

declarations.name: indexOf
limitations: The collection indexOf()/indexOfFirst()/indexOfLast() family is List-oriented; there is no String-specific overload

declarations.name: repeat
limitations: Same name collision risk as the top-level kotlin.repeat() — repeat is a Lua keyword

declarations.name: toCharArray
limitations: No Char type exists in this subset at all, so this has no meaningful target representation

declarations.name: templates
declarations.documentation: String templates — both bare $identifier and ${expression} interpolation — join via Lua's .. with tostring()-wrapping of non-literal parts

declarations.name: rawStrings
limitations: Triple-quoted """...""" raw/multi-line strings aren't lexed at all
